title: [GA4] Event naming rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Event and parameter names are case sensitive, start with a letter and use letters, numbers and underscores; reserved names and prefixes (_, firebase_, ga_, google_, gtag.).

title: [GA4] Event collection limits
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Event and parameter names 40 characters; parameter values 100 (page_title 300, page_referrer 420, page_location 1,000); 25 parameters per event; 25 user properties; key events with names over 40 characters are not reported as key events.

title: Recommended events (GA4 events reference)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Recommended event names for all businesses, online sales and lead generation (generate_lead, qualify_lead, working_lead, disqualify_lead, close_convert_lead, close_unconvert_lead); purchase needs transaction_id, value excluding shipping and tax, currency when value is set, and items.

title: [GA4] About key events
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Key events defined; Google Ads conversions are created from key events and shared back to Analytics; from 15 June 2026 Consent Mode (in Google Ads) is the single control for Google Ads cookies and identifiers, replacing the Google signals setting for this purpose.

title: [GA4] URL builders: Collect campaign data with custom URLs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Supported UTM parameters; always use utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign; utm_id and utm_source_platform recommended; utm_creative_format and utm_marketing_tactic not currently reported; values are case sensitive and lowercase is recommended; missing values show as (not set).

title: [GA4] Default channel group
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Channel rules: paid regex ^(.*cp.*|ppc|retargeting|paid.*)$; Email, Referral, Affiliates, Display, Organic Social and Direct conditions; Unassigned when no rule matches; rules not case sensitive; AI Assistant channel (medium ai-assistant), excluding Google AI Overviews and AI Mode.

title: [GA4] Identify unwanted referrals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Exclude domains such as payment processors from referral credit; up to 50 per web stream; Editor role; automatic self-referral detection for own domains and linked cross-domain visits.

title: [GA4] Get started with attribution (attribution models)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Three models (data-driven attribution, paid and organic last click, Google paid channels last click); first click, linear, time decay and position-based removed November 2023; how data-driven attribution compares exposed and similar holdback users; direct visits get no credit unless the whole path is direct.

title: [GA4] Select attribution settings
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reporting model changes apply to historical and future data; lookback 30 days by default (or 7) for first_visit and first_open, 90 days by default (or 30 or 60) for other key events, applied going forward; GA4 reports default to paid and organic channels, Google Ads reports to Google paid channels.

title: [GA4] Data retention
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Standard properties keep user- and event-level data for 2 or 14 months; 360 adds 26, 38 or 50 months for event data; the setting affects explorations and funnel reports only.

title: [GA4] BigQuery Export
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Standard properties have a daily export limit of 1 million events; streaming export is best-effort; daily tables can update for up to two days; use the daily export for attribution; free BigQuery sandbox with charges beyond its limits.

title: [GA4] Behavioral modeling for consent mode
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Prerequisites: advanced consent mode, at least 1,000 events a day with analytics_storage denied for at least 7 days, and at least 1,000 daily users with consent granted on 7 of the previous 28 days; Blended reporting identity; modelled data not in BigQuery export or retention reports.

title: Consent mode overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. The four consent types (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization); basic implementation blocks tags until consent; advanced sends cookieless pings while denied and allows advertiser-specific modelling.

title: Data protection and online privacy (cookies)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Last checked by the EU 05/08/2026. Websites must get consent before installing cookies; exemptions for cookies used only to transmit a communication or strictly needed for a service the user requested.

title: Data discrepancies: Factors and troubleshooting
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Why Google Ads and other tools differ: conversions reported on the ad interaction date, 24 to 48 hour sync, conversions up to 90 days after the click, lookback windows, count settings, primary and secondary actions, modelled cross-device, view-through outside the Conversions column, invalid traffic, Ads counting only its own interactions.

title: About Conversion Lift
supports: Opened with WebFetch. User-based and geography-based Conversion Lift; reported metrics such as incremental conversions, iCPA and iROAS; not available for all Google Ads accounts.

title: Ads MCP server tools: A/B tests and conversion lift studies
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Meta ads MCP server tools to create conversion lift studies and read their status and results, plus A/B test create, read and update tools and an eligibility check.

title: Looker Studio is now Data Studio
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 11 April 2026. Looker Studio renamed Data Studio; free Data Studio and paid Data Studio Pro; existing reports and data sources moved over with no action.

title: Incremental Clicks Impact of Search Advertising (Chan, Yuan, Koehler and Kumar, 2011)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Over 400 search ads pause studies; on average 89% of paid clicks were not replaced by organic clicks when ads were paused; modelled estimate averaged across verticals.

title: Measuring Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments (Vaver and Koehler, 2011)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Geo experiments randomly assign non-overlapping regions to control or treatment; conceptually simple and easy to interpret.

title: Inferring causal impact using Bayesian structural time-series models (Brodersen, Gallusser, Koehler, Remy and Scott, 2015)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. CausalImpact: a state-space model that predicts the counterfactual from control time series (synthetic controls) when a randomised experiment is not available; R package.

title: The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising (Lewis and Rao, 2015)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Abstract read on the publisher page: 25 large field experiments; coefficient of variation of individual sales of about 10 is common; informative experiments can need more than 10 million person-weeks; median confidence interval on ROI over 100 percentage points wide.

title: Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement (Gordon, Moakler and Zettelmeyer)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 663 randomised experiments at Facebook; median experimental lifts 29%, 18% and 5% (upper, middle, lower funnel); double machine learning estimated 83%, 58%, 24% and stratified propensity score matching 173%, 176%, 64%.

title: Bayesian Methods for Media Mix Modeling with Carryover and Shape Effects (Jin, Wang, Sun, Chan and Koehler, 2017)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. MMM with carryover and diminishing-returns shape; Bayesian priors; with small samples priors drive the posterior and can bias estimates; optimal media mix has high variance.

title: About the Meridian project
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Open-source Bayesian MMM for causal estimates; geo-level data; reach and frequency inputs; priors from business knowledge; controls such as Google Query Volume; outputs ROI, response curves and budget scenarios.

title: ROI priors and calibration (Meridian)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page. Turning experiments into ROI priors (CalibrationBuilder); MMM counterfactual is zero spend, so reduced-spend tests do not map directly; check prior against posterior.

title: Analyst's Guide to MMM (Robyn)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Footer 2024. At least two years of weekly data (four to five if monthly); about one variable per ten observations; exposure over spend; geometric adstock ranges (TV 0.3-0.8, OOH/print/radio 0.1-0.4, digital 0-0.3); Hill saturation; ridge regression; NRMSE and DECOMP.RSSD; calibrate with lift tests; analyst selects the model.

title: GeoLift (GitHub repository)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Geo-level lift measurement with synthetic control methods; market selection with power calculators; inference and plots; requires R 4.0 or newer.

title: PyMC-Marketing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Open-source (Apache-2.0) Python library: MMM with adstock, saturation, lift-test calibration and budget optimisation; customer lifetime value models.

title: Google Analytics MCP server (GitHub repository)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. MCP server for Google Analytics APIs; reporting, funnel, realtime and admin read tools; write tools (property annotations, custom dimensions, key events) only with --allow-write and the analytics.edit scope; Apache-2.0.
